summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with long-standing epilepsy, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, ischemic cardiomyopathy, and a history of stroke and line infections, was admitted after experiencing a seizure during dialysis, followed by hypotension requiring norepinephrine. He was stabilized in the MICU, where concerns for sepsis were ruled out by negative cultures. His seizure was attributed to fluid shifts and possible suboptimal antiepileptic drug levels, though trough levels remained pending. A previously functional AV graft was found to be thrombosed; attempts at thrombectomy and angioplasty failed, leading to placement of a tunneled femoral dialysis catheter. The patient developed a mild contrast reaction during imaging, managed with antihistamines and steroids. He was started on midodrine for dialysis-associated hypotension and educated on strict adherence to his antiepileptic regimen, including morning and post-dialysis doses. He remained seizure-free, hemodynamically stable, and was discharged home with services, with follow-up arranged with neurology, vascular surgery, and primary care.
